evidence_lineage_contract_v1.relation: Owns Stage 5 lineage comparison semantics. Graph Evolution binds an externally supplied Stage 5 lineage digest and reuses this exact frozen contract resource digest without defining another Stage 5 lineage model.

graph_contract_v1.relation: The existing validate_graph_contract owner alone validates target Graph structure, topology, permission vocabulary, generation, and semantic digest. Graph Evolution consumes that result and does not redefine or copy Graph semantics.

graph_schema_v1.relation: Proposal target_graph references the existing Graph schema identity. This contract carries no duplicate Graph definition.

operations.ADD_CORRECTIVE: Add exactly one required CORRECTIVE_AUTHORIZED node. The digest-bound Request must identify the observed finding, accepted root-cause record, and at least one evidence reference.
operations.ADD_VERIFICATION: Add exactly one READ_ONLY_REVIEW verification node while preserving every parent node and verifier.
operations.ADD_INVESTIGATION: Add exactly one optional READ_ONLY_REVIEW investigation node. It cannot enter a required join; any join that references it must be first-success.
operations.SPLIT_PENDING: Add exactly one split node for a Request subject asserted PENDING. The subject remains byte-for-byte unchanged, the split preserves role, permission, verifier, and classification, and gates cannot change.
operations.DISABLE_OPTIONAL_PENDING: Remove exactly one optional Request subject asserted PENDING. The subject cannot be referenced by a required join or gate; only a first-success reference may be removed with it.
operations.NO_CHANGE: Explicitly recommend retaining the parent Graph. NO_CHANGE has no target_graph, target_generation, or target_graph_digest.

binding.request_and_proposal: Each Request and Proposal binds operation, Graph ID, parent generation and existing Graph semantic digest, external authority, proposer node/role/permission, subject node, change class, closed reason code, bounded evidence and decision references, bounded affected paths, and Stage 5 lineage digest.
binding.decision_chain: The pure validate_decision_chain operation validates all five documents, recomputes their canonical digests, binds Proposal to Request and PM Preauthorization, binds Acceptance to Proposal, PM authority, and the preauthorized independent evaluator, binds Result to the complete chain, and compares the supplied parent Graph with the inert target Graph. It performs no apply or execution.
binding.generation_lineage: Every changed Proposal target generation is exactly parent_generation plus one and the Graph owner must reproduce graph_id, target_generation, and target_graph_digest. NO_CHANGE crosses no generation.
binding.completed_history: Pure parent/target differencing preserves every unaffected parent node byte-for-byte, preserves split subjects byte-for-byte, and forbids changes to human_gates or completion_verifier. SPLIT_PENDING and DISABLE_OPTIONAL_PENDING require a digest-bound PENDING assertion because Graph Contract v1 intentionally contains no runtime node status. The validator never obtains or dereferences runtime state.

pm_preauthorization.closed_world: Allowed operations, change classes, nodes, roles, permissions, path patterns, generation budget, all six per-operation budgets, independent evaluator, stop conditions, and Project Manager authority are explicit closed fields. Missing or unlisted values are denied.
pm_preauthorization.budget_alignment: Every allowed operation has a positive remaining budget and every disallowed operation has zero budget. When remaining_generations is zero, all five mutating operation budgets must be zero; NO_CHANGE may retain a positive budget. Generation and operation budgets are inclusive bounded counters and confer no authority after exhaustion.
pm_preauthorization.ordinary_scope: C0 and C1 can be listed for ordinary preauthorized continuation. C2 or C3 may be represented only when Project Manager authority explicitly lists them; classification never upgrades itself.
pm_preauthorization.stop_rule: The complete fail-stop set is mandatory: budget exhaustion, no progress, evaluator rejection, authority change, contract change, permission expansion, and gate or verifier removal.

canonical_digest.construction: For kind K, SHA-256(UTF-8('sagekit-graph-evolution-' + K + '-v1') + NUL + canonical strict JSON document bytes). A digest exists only after complete kind-specific validation.
canonical_digest.normalization: Object keys sort by logical Unicode scalar sequence; arrays preserve supplied order; UTF-8 has no BOM or insignificant whitespace; integers use shortest decimal form; mandatory JSON escapes are fixed; all other Unicode scalars encode directly. Duplicate object names, non-integer numbers, non-JSON values, cycles, and lone UTF-16 surrogates are invalid.
canonical_digest.distinctions: Document digests bind complete validated contract documents. They are not Graph semantic identity, Stage 5 lineage identity, authority, permission, acceptance, execution identity, or resource-integrity digests.

strict_validation.unknown_fields: Every document and nested control object rejects unknown fields. No extension bag, free-form metadata, or arbitrary content field exists.
strict_validation.reference_boundary: Authority, evidence, decision, and document references are bounded repository-neutral strings and reject absolute, rooted, drive-prefixed, UNC, any URI-scheme-prefixed, backslash, and newline forms.
strict_validation.path_boundary: Affected paths and allowed path patterns are repository-relative slash-separated values. They reject roots, drives, URIs, backslashes, newlines, empty segments, current or parent traversal segments, and trailing slashes.
strict_validation.opaque_identity_boundary: Graph, authority, node, and role identities are bounded opaque strings inherited from the Stage 4 identity model. They may look like paths or URIs and are never opened, normalized as locations, traversed, or dereferenced; appearance alone is not grounds for rejection.
strict_validation.allowlist_boundary: Operations, change classes, Graph-owned permission names, reason codes, evaluator decisions, stop conditions, outcomes, messages, document kinds, and errors are closed enumerations.

failure_semantics.INPUT_INVALID: Malformed strict JSON, duplicate object names, invalid Unicode, unknown fields, schema mismatch, bound violation other than aggregate bytes, or conditional mismatch.
failure_semantics.INPUT_TOO_LARGE: The complete canonical document exceeds its kind-specific byte budget.
failure_semantics.GRAPH_INVALID: A changed Proposal target_graph fails the existing Graph owner validation.
failure_semantics.GRAPH_BINDING_MISMATCH: A valid target Graph does not reproduce Proposal Graph ID, target generation, or target_graph_digest.
failure_semantics.RESULT_ERROR_EXCLUSIVITY: Exactly one complete Result or one complete Error is required.
failure_semantics.bounded_errors: Errors contain at most 100 closed machine issues and never echo arbitrary invalid values, private content, a partial Proposal, or a target Graph.

semantic_boundaries.proposal_inertness: A Proposal does not grant permission or authority, does not execute any node, and does not mutate, create, activate, persist, or apply a Graph generation.
semantic_boundaries.acceptance_boundary: Acceptance is an external digest-bound decision record. Proposal presence alone is never acceptance; evaluator approval alone is never Project Manager authority.
semantic_boundaries.apply_ownership: The independently authorized host retains all apply ownership and must revalidate current parent Graph, authority, budgets, stop conditions, acceptance, and target Graph before any later application.
semantic_boundaries.result_error_exclusivity: A valid outcome contains exactly one complete Result or exactly one complete Error. Error never masquerades as rejection, no-change success, or partial acceptance.
semantic_boundaries.privacy: The closed schemas provide no dedicated fields for prompts, reasoning traces, transcripts, environment dumps, credentials, commands, callbacks, arbitrary payloads, or mutable handles. This is a structural data-minimization boundary, not a claim that opaque identity strings have been inspected or proven non-sensitive. Producers must not place secrets or private content in opaque identities. Reference and path fields separately reject absolute local paths and URI locations.
semantic_boundaries.non_goals: This contract adds no command interface, scheduling component, database, network API, filesystem traversal, process launch, runtime writer, proposal builder, Graph apply implementation, or later-stage adapter behavior.

digest_semantics: canonical_sha256 values in resources and dependencies are LF-normalized resource-integrity digests only. The canonical_digest section separately owns Graph Evolution document digests. Neither digest family grants authority or execution.
compatibility: Graph Evolution Contract v1 is additive and execution-inert. It consumes the frozen Stage 5 contract resource digest and the existing Graph owner without changing their schemas, digest domains, semantic projections, topology, status, permission, gate, verifier, lineage, runtime, or apply semantics.

packaged_mirror.expectation: All seven resources are byte-identical mirrors of canonical resources in docs/contracts/graph-evolution/v1.
